*   **Pose Estimation Accuracy:** Inaccurate pose estimation negatively impacts reconstruction results [S2].

The claim states that inaccurate pose estimation negatively impacts reconstruction results. The provided text from Source [S2] explicitly contains the sentence: '为了提高对新姿态和形状的泛化能力，研究人员引入 SMPL 作为结构化几何体嵌入，但不准确的 SMPL 估计会对重建结果产生负面影响' (To improve generalization to new poses and shapes, researchers introduced SMPL as a structured geometry embedding, but inaccurate SMPL estimation will have a negative impact on reconstruction results). Since SMPL is a parametric human model used for pose and shape estimation, this directly supports the claim.
supported
*   **When to use:** It should be used when synthesizing novel views of dynamic human avatars from sparse multi-view video data is required [S1, S2].

The claim states that the method should be used for synthesizing novel views of dynamic human avatars from sparse multi-view video data. Source [S2] explicitly states that the method 'Neural body' was proposed 'to synthesize new views of dynamic characters from sparse multi-view videos' (用于从稀疏多视角视频中合成动态人物的新视角). Source [S1] corroborates this by describing Neural Body as applying NeRF volume rendering to 'human avatars with moving poses from videos' and noting that it was able to 'interpolate between frames and between poses'. Both sources confirm the specific application scenario mentioned in the claim.

Render via volumetric integration [S1, S2].

The claim states that the method involves 'Render via volumetric integration'. Source [S1] explicitly states that 'Neural Body [63] applied NeRF volume rendering to human avatars'. Source [S2] describes the same method (Neural Body) as an 'implicit neural representation method for synthesizing new views', which is the definition of volumetric rendering/integration in the context of NeRF. Both sources confirm that the rendering technique used is volume-based (NeRF volume rendering).

This matches all facts in the claim: the method name (Neural Body), the authors (Peng et al.), the year (2021), and the function (synthesizing new views of dynamic characters from sparse multi-view videos).
